decision.reason: Arm AI Portal is a fresh, exact-timestamped and non-duplicate developer-tool launch. The live catalogue and MCP documentation support a bounded account of what is available, while independent sustained-load research supports a practical decision: shortlist by model, runtime and target, then test the complete deployment system.

claims.text: Arm AI Portal brings together optimized models, target information, performance data, code examples and deployment workflows.
claims.sourceLocator: s1 opening and launch scope; s2 live model comparison; s3 model and deployment sections

claims.text: The public comparison view showed 84 results when checked on 8 September 2026.
claims.sourceLocator: Live Explore/Compare view text: 84 results

claims.text: The portal supports filtering by task, device class, runtime and format, and comparison using benchmark score, latency, peak memory and average memory.
claims.sourceLocator: s2 filter and compare view; s3 model-comparison section

claims.text: Arm says individual model entries can include training-data provenance, benchmark conditions, runtime and test-device information.
claims.sourceLocator: Model comparison and provenance section

claims.text: Launch examples include Qwen, Gemma and YOLO model families using ExecuTorch, LiteRT and ONNX Runtime.
claims.sourceLocator: s1 Start faster section; s3 initial models section

claims.text: Arm reports more than a fourfold Qwen3-TTS speed-up on a vivo X300 using single-thread execution, a Q8_0 talker with a code predictor, mixed quantisation and SME2 acceleration.
claims.sourceLocator: Start faster performance bullets

claims.text: Arm reports more than 40 percent performance improvement for YOLO26n using single-thread FP16 versus FP32 on vivo X300 with SME2, and mixed FP16 and INT8 quantisation versus FP32 on Raspberry Pi 5 with NEON.
claims.sourceLocator: Start faster performance bullets

claims.text: Index Us did not reproduce Arm's reported performance figures.
claims.sourceLocator: Declared reporting limitation; sources contain Arm measurements only

claims.text: Bring-your-own-model optimization is offered through an early-access program rather than as general availability.
claims.sourceLocator: s1 availability paragraph; s3 early-access sections

claims.text: The public portal page publishes MCP setup commands for Codex, Claude Code and GitHub Copilot and a Streamable HTTP endpoint.
claims.sourceLocator: MCP Server section of live model comparison view

claims.text: Arm's launch announcement describes agent-ready AI resources as early access ahead of general release.
claims.sourceLocator: Opening availability paragraph

claims.text: The Arm technical post describes optimization as involving model export, operator mapping, graph changes, kernel selection and quantization, with runtime choice affecting performance.
claims.sourceLocator: Optimization workflow section

claims.text: The independent preprint tested one 4-bit Qwen 2.5 1.5B model on four platforms for 20 warm-condition iterations.
claims.sourceLocator: v2 abstract and methods

claims.text: In the independent experiment, iPhone throughput fell 41.5 percent from peak and settled near 23.7 tokens per second, while a tuned S24 configuration declined about 15 percent and settled near 10 tokens per second.
claims.sourceLocator: Results and conclusion; iPhone and S24 sections

claims.text: The independent experiment's NPU configuration was slower but stable under sustained load, while the laptop result was constrained by battery power.
claims.sourceLocator: Results, deployment-suitability discussion and conclusion

claims.text: The paper used different inference frameworks and quantization formats across devices and different power-measurement boundaries, limiting direct platform comparisons.
claims.sourceLocator: Section 5.4 Framework heterogeneity and Power measurement methodology

claims.text: The independent paper does not evaluate Arm AI Portal and cannot confirm Arm's portal-specific optimization claims.
claims.sourceLocator: Different studied systems and dates; boundary stated explicitly in the article

claims.text: A portal result should be treated as evidence for a shortlist, not proof that the model will meet production requirements on another device or software stack.
claims.sourceLocator: Portal comparison scope plus s4's platform, framework and sustained-load limitations

claims.text: A reproducible local evaluation should retain the source checkpoint, converted artifact, runtime and backend, quantization, target device and workload conditions.
claims.sourceLocator: Synthesis of s3 optimization steps and s4 validity limits

claims.text: Local acceptance testing should include task quality, cold and warm latency, sustained throughput, memory, power or battery effects, temperature and failures where those measures matter to the product.
claims.sourceLocator: Index Us recommendation based on portal comparison dimensions and s4 sustained-load methodology
